circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. It became the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Located in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, this street circuit encircles Albert Park Lake and hosts the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside supporting racing series including the Supercars Championship event. The track holds the highest FIA safety classification for its facilities and infrastructure.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit has a storied history hosting the Austrian Grand Prix across two distinct periods: first as the Österreichring from 1970-1987, then following modifications and a name change to the A1-Ring, it returned to the championship calendar from 1997-2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street-racing venue in Azerbaijan's capital, positioned along the city's waterfront boulevard and measuring 6. 003 km per lap, ranking as the fourth-longest track in Formula One. The circuit hosted its first F1 race as the 2016 European Grand Prix before being renamed the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the first Formula One race held in the Middle East that same year and continues to stage the annual Bahrain Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track has accommodated various motorsport categories including GP2 racing, drag racing, and 24-hour endurance competitions, along with Australian V8 Supercars from 2006 to 2010.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile venue for motorsport competition. The facility holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km Belgian circuit located near the town of Spa that has been a cornerstone of Formula One racing since 1950, when it featured in the sport's inaugural season. The track has maintained an uninterrupted presence on the Grand Prix calendar from 1985 onwards, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006, and continues to host the annual Belgian Grand Prix.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, this 4. 361-kilometre circuit serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond hosting top-tier single-seater racing, the venue has accommodated various international motorsport series including prototype and touring car championships throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport venue hosted the Formula One Chinese Grand Prix intermittently from 2004 through 2019 and resumed from 2024 onward. The facility has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing events alongside its primary Formula One championship.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone Circuit, located in England near Northamptonshire, has hosted the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably staged the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After rotating among three venues between 1955 and 1986, the Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards, while the track also accommodates the MotoGP British round.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in a communist country when it debuted in 1986, constructed in just eight months, which was faster than any previous Formula One circuit build. Located in Mogyoród outside the capital, the 4. 381 km track was built near a major highway after plans for a Monaco-style street circuit in Budapest's central park were rejected by the Hungarian government.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km Italian racing venue constructed in 1922 near Milan, making it Europe's oldest permanent circuit and the third of its kind globally. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949 (except during 1980 renovations), the track earns its "Temple of Speed" nickname through its characteristic long straights and fast corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: The Suzuka Circuit, situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, is a 5. 807 km motorsport facility operated by Honda Mobilityland with a spectator capacity of 155,000. The track is renowned for hosting prestigious Formula One races alongside the Japanese Super Formula championship.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding thoroughfares. The track winds past iconic destinations such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, making it one of racing's most visually distinctive urban venues.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit in Mexico City honoring brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both of whom died in racing accidents in the 1960s and early 1970s. The track has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix during two earlier periods with a different layout, with the most recent interruption ending in 2015 when the event returned.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, spanning 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and an average qualifying speed of approximately 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One racing, the venue joined the championship calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street circuit that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, following the waterfront of the Principality of Monaco. Though officially named after the principality itself, it is widely known as the Monte Carlo circuit due to its primary location within that particular neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes northwest of Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that rejoined the Formula One calendar in 2021 to host the Netherlands Grand Prix after a lengthy absence. The venue's involvement with Formula One is scheduled to conclude following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Qatari racing facility situated north of Doha near the city of Lusail, spanning 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing circuit in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal plane crash. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features an associated kart facility named after fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has been the home of the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural running in 2021. The circuit also began hosting a major electric racing series event from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: Singapore's Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through the city's Downtown Core and Kallang districts, making it one of the few urban venues on the Formula One calendar that races around the waterfront precinct.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit features a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test of both speed and handling. With FIA Grade 1 certification and seating for over 140,000 spectators, the track serves as a premier venue for international motorsport competition.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas near Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that currently hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside NASCAR and motorcycle racing events. The venue has also accommodated various other racing series over its history, including IndyCar and sports car championships.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai and British racing driver competing for Williams in Formula One under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006, along with 32 race victories throughout his 23-season career. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, winning the 2018–19 World Endurance Championship, two Le Mans 24-hour races, and the 2019 Daytona 24-hour event, making him the sole driver to claim titles in both Formula One and world sportscar championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli has been competing in Formula One for Mercedes since his 2025 debut, during which he has secured six Grand Prix victories.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor currently driving for the Haas team in Formula One racing.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian motorsport talent Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One, representing the Audi team as his competitive platform in the sport's premier category.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas, a Finnish driver, currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after establishing himself as a consistent competitor over 13 seasons. His career highlights include two runner-up championship finishes with Mercedes in consecutive years and a total of 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One for Alpine. He represents his country on the international motorsport stage at the pinnacle of single-seater racing.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, currently holds a reserve role with Haas in Formula One while competing in the European Le Mans Series' LMP2 category for Nielsen Racing. He has made seven Grand Prix appearances between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri remains a significant achievement in his racing career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: French-Algerian driver Isack Alexandre Hadjar races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, representing France in international competition.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding a record-tying seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. He leads multiple statistical categories in the sport, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved success in endurance motorsport, claiming victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand motorsport competitor, drives for Racing Bulls in the Formula One championship.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a driver from Monaco, currently races for Ferrari in Formula One. He finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship and has accumulated nine race victories over his nine seasons in the sport.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish motorsport competitor currently racing in the World Endurance Championship with BMW through WRT, while also taking on select NASCAR Cup Series duties with Trackhouse Racing. The driver previously competed in Formula One across two separate stints from 2014-2020 and 2022-2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British competitor in Formula One, secured the drivers' championship in 2025 while driving for McLaren. Throughout his eight seasons in the sport, he has claimed victory in 12 Grand Prix events.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. Earlier in his career, he secured a victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 15-season career that includes six Grand Prix victories. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while competing for Red Bull Racing.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver, races for McLaren in Formula One, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories during his four-year tenure in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger", he concluded his time in the sport in 2024.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell has secured seven victories during his eight-year Formula One career and currently races for Mercedes.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz has competed in Formula One for over a decade, securing four Grand Prix victories during his career. He currently races for Williams in the championship.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant competed in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery for Era Motorsport in IMSA competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin in the sport's premier championship.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently serving as a reserve for both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls after competing in Formula One between 2021 and 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch racing driver Max Verstappen has secured four consecutive Formula One world titles between 2021 and 2024 while representing Red Bull Racing. His achievements include 71 Grand Prix victories accumulated over his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver who holds the distinction of being the only driver from China to participate in Formula One, competing in the series from 2022 through 2024. He currently works as a reserve driver for the Cadillac Formula One team.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Alpine Racing operates from Enstone as Renault's works team, rebranded from Renault F1 Team in 2021 to showcase the French manufacturer's sports car division before Renault's Formula One departure at the end of 2025. The team has secured one victory during its Alpine era, courtesy of Esteban Ocon's triumph at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, and currently competes with Mercedes powerunits and a French racing licence.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automaker, has maintained a presence in Formula One through different organizational structures, with the current incarnation operating under AMR GP Limited and competing under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's longest-surviving and most accomplished team, fielding cars in every World Championship since the sport's inception in 1950. The outfit, colloquially referred to as the Prancing Horse after its iconic emblem, represents the sport's most storied and successful franchise.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: American-licensed Haas F1 Team was founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas in 2014 and entered Formula One competition in 2016. Ayao Komatsu currently leads the team as principal, taking over from Guenther Steiner who departed in early 2024 after overseeing the operation since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: The Swiss engineering firm Sauber Motorsport, established in 1970 by Peter Sauber, initially built sports cars before transitioning to Formula One machinery as a privateer constructor. The operation competed in the championship from 1993 onward, securing two world endurance titles and a Le Mans 24 Hours victory en route, before ceasing operations in 2025 as one of the sport's longest-serving independent teams. Audi acquired the company and its infrastructure in 2024 to serve as the technical foundation for its Formula One entry.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that operates as a division of the McLaren Group. The team is entirely owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company and competes under corporate sponsorship in the sport.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with the current iteration operating as Mercedes-AMG Petronas from Brackley under a German licence. The team restructured in 2022 to establish equal ownership between Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff. The outfit is traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows" due to its heritage and iconic silver livery.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor established in 2024, operating as Red Bull GmbH's second factory team alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the squad represents the conglomerate's expansion of constructors competing in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad serves as Red Bull's second outfit in the sport.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England and owned by Red Bull GmbH. Founded in 2005 under Christian Horner's leadership, the team operated under his management until 2025, when Laurent Mekies assumed the role of team principal. Red Bull GmbH also operates a second Formula One outfit through Racing Bulls.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and has established itself as a significant presence in the sport's history.
